title: Telemetry bridge for token pressure & latency SLOs (VPC health checks)
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Summary:
Build a lightweight telemetry bridge and Terraform primitives to standardize VPC health probes for token throughput, request latencies (P50/P95/P99), error-rate windows, and saturation indicators. The goal is to provide consistent SLO evaluation across private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and integrate alerts and dashboards with the central observability stack while keeping network/tenant isolation requirements intact.

Motivation & Goals:
- Many private deployments currently emit inconsistent probe metrics across edge workers; alert fatigue and missed saturation events observed during customer upgrades.
- Provide a reproducible Terraform module that wires probes, RBAC, and secure forwarding for telemetry without opening broad inbound endpoints.
- Implement a "telemetry-bridge" agent (small sidecar or daemonset) that aggregates local probes and forwards to central Prometheus Pushgateway or remote_write with per-customer tenancy tags.
- Define canonical SLO rules and Alertmanager policies for: latency (P99 > threshold), error-rate (> x% over rolling window), token throughput (tokens/s falling below watermarks), and saturation (queue depth, GPU util, dispatch latency).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Push vs pull: remote_write is preferred for scalability, but for air-gapped clusters we support an authenticated Pushgateway-style relay.
- Aggregation window: 60s windows for token throughput and saturation gauges; 5m rolling error-rate to avoid noisy flaps.
- Tagging: include tenant_id, deployment_id, model_variant in every metric to enable routed alerting and per-route dashboards.
- Backpressure handling: probes should support burst-resistant counters and path for graceful degradation (fall back to local logging) if connectivity to central stack fails.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Terraform module (private/telemetry-module): resources to deploy telemetry-bridge, ServiceAccount, KMS secret reference, ConfigMap for probe rules, and optional Service/Ingress for push relay.
2) telemetry-bridge agent: Go microservice with pluggable exporters (remote_write, pushgateway). Exposes metrics locally on 127.0.0.1:9100 and a health endpoint for k8s readiness/liveness.
3) SLO rules: PromQL recipes, Alertmanager routes and templates, and JSON policies consumed by Console for per-route SLO views.
4) Dashboards: create Grafana dashboards (vpc/token-pressure, vpc/latency-slos) and Console integration for token-watermark visualizations.
5) Runbook and rollout: canary on dedicated account -> staged rollout -> full rollout with automated abort thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module deploys telemetry-bridge in a brand-new VPC cluster (tested in staging) without manual steps.
- Central Prometheus receives token throughput, latency histograms, error-rate windows, and saturation metrics with correct tenant tags.
- Alertmanager fires an incident when synthetic probe P99 latency breaches SLO for 2 consecutive 5m windows in canary.
- Dashboards display token-watermark and saturation gauges; Console per-route SLO page shows computed burn rates.

Operational considerations:
- Costs: remote_write retention downstream must be limited for private tier customers; default retention 7d for SLO metrics.
- Security: all outbound connections use mTLS and per-tenant certificates; Terraform module wires KMS references and rotation policy.
- Observability: instrumentation includes histograms for latency, monotonic counters for tokens, and sampled traces for probe failures.

Open questions / risks:
- For air-gapped on-prem, relaying metrics via a manual transfer process increases furniture to support—need playbook with Support.
- Threshold tuning: we need per-customer baselines. Plan to provide automated baseline estimator (follow-up ticket).

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Telemetry+Bridge+Design
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-bridge/pull/123 (agent), https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/88 (module)
